key_insight: Glioma appears to leave a detectable transcriptional signature in circulating CD14+ monocytes, enabling blood-based detection and recurrence monitoring with machine learning.
clinical_relevance: This approach could support non-invasive glioma screening, postoperative surveillance, and risk stratification alongside standard imaging and pathology.
method: Single-cell RNA sequencing of blood immune cells identified glioma-associated changes in circulating CD14+ monocytes.
Transcriptomic features from CD14+ monocytes were used to train an ensemble machine learning diagnostic model.
The model was tested in independent cohorts for glioma detection and postoperative recurrence monitoring.
evidence_signal: The model achieved a mean cross-validated AUC of 0.975 in training, AUC 0.888 in an independent cohort of 567 participants, and AUC 0.975 for recurrence detection in 51 postoperative samples.
watch_item: Prospective multicenter validation and standardized blood-processing workflows are still needed before clinical implementation.
paper_title: Sensitive Glioma Detection and Recurrence Monitoring Using a Machine Learning Model Based on Circulating Monocytes
